findings.quote: Fidelity does not publish a robo-advisor price on the pages that could be read.  /  Fidelity publishing a robo-advisor price would add a third published robo figure next to Schwab and Ally.  /  Fidelity does not publish a robo-advisor price on the pages that could be read, so Ally and Schwab are the two brokers here with published robo minimums and fees.
findings.problem: Contradicted by Fidelity's own site: https://www.fidelity.com/managed-accounts/fidelity-go/overview (readable today) says Fidelity Go has $0 advisory fees under $25,000 and 0.35% per year at $25,000 and above, no minimum to open and $10 minimum balance to invest. The sources file only tried the /go/overview URL (HTTP 502) and gave up. Three places state or imply Fidelity has no published robo price; the 'Not For' bullet comparing Schwab $5,000 and Ally $100 also omits the $10 Fidelity Go figure.
findings.fix: Add Fidelity Go ($0 advisory fee under $25,000, 0.35% a year above, $10 minimum balance) to the Fidelity row, robo paragraph, Ally section, Not-For bullet and What-Would-Change list, and delete the 'does not publish' claims.

findings.quote: Fidelity charges $49.95 when no transaction fee (NTF) non-Fidelity funds are sold within 60 days of purchase.

findings.fix: Rewrite as 'Fidelity fits poorly for people who trade no-transaction-fee funds on short holds, since non-Fidelity NTF funds charge $49.95 on redemption within 60 days.'
